findings.location: ## Open problem: paragraphs beginning “The perturbative comparison data are fixed as follows” and “The theory also has a local symmetric stress-energy tensor”; title “Four-dimensional Yang–Mills existence and mass gap”.
findings.evidence: Jaffe–Witten §4 (MPPc printed pp. 141–142; standalone PDF §4, p. 6) states broad short-distance agreement with asymptotic freedom and perturbative renormalization, including a stress tensor and an OPE with prescribed local singularities. The item adds specific all-order little-o remainders for correlations and Wilson coefficients, a dimension-truncation scaling-degree bound, and a cutoff-independent spacetime-smearing limit for the stress tensor. The cited formulation does not state these quantitative conditions or establish their equivalence to its broad requirements. Unless supported as equivalent, they define a strengthened problem while the title presents the Clay problem without qualification.

The contract assigns the fixed-axis argument to item step 1.1 and also attributes angle endpoints to step 1.1. The current item’s step 1.1 proves quaternion product and norm identities; its fixed-axis and rotation-angle argument is in step 2.1, while central kernel values are treated in steps 1.2 and 3.1. These internal evidence locators do not match the item.

coverage_note: Reviewed both assigned pages, all three assigned item bodies, the current batch proof-contract record, and the empty cross-batch dependency record; no item dependencies were declared. Checked cited primary-source passages for the Clay statement and status, pure-gauge beta coefficients, and Osterwalder–Schrader regularity context. I did not reconstruct the full all-order renormalization/OPE theory or the full reconstruction proof; the relationship between the item’s quantitative short-distance conditions and the canonical Clay formulation remains unresolved and is reported as suspected.
